title: Windows & Doors Google Business Profile
html:
Google Business Profile Management for Window and Door Companies

A strong window and door profile wins on four things Google can check: the right categories, fresh install photos, recent reviews and an accurate service area.

Categories and services

Pick "Window installation service" as the primary category, then add door installation and replacement as secondaries. List replacement windows, entry doors, patio doors and storm doors as separate services, so the profile matches how homeowners search for each job.

  • Primary category choice
  • Secondary categories
  • Services by job type
  • Product line descriptions

Install photos and posts

Every finished install is a photo set. A bay window project in March earns a post before spring replacement calls start.

  • Before and after sets
  • City-tagged posts
  • Seasonal offer posts
  • Crew and van photos

Review requests after install

Review count and recency help decide who the map pack shows first.

  • Post-install text request
  • Direct review link
  • Replies to every review
  • Spam review reporting

Service area and listings

  • Service area by zip
  • Name, address, phone match
  • Duplicate listing cleanup
  • Citation submissions

How We Run Google Business Profile for Window and Door Companies

This is when it happens, from the first audit to the monthly report that shows what the profile produced.

Report and Decide

You get calls and booked estimates from the profile, plus review count and map pack position for your main searches.

Google Business Profile vs Local Services Ads

A Google Business Profile and Local Services Ads reach the same homeowner in different ways. The profile earns map clicks over time, while Local Services Ads charge per lead. Most window and door companies start with the profile because it supports every paid channel, including Google Ads.

Is a Google Business Profile Right for Your Window or Door Company?

Start now if the basics are in place. Wait if a fix would eat the first months.

Start now if

  • You have an address or service area Google accepts
  • You can send a review request after every install
  • You have recent install photos to upload
  • Someone answers calls during your listed hours

Wait if

  • Your business name or phone number changes next month
  • Nobody can answer or return calls quickly
  • You cannot take more estimates this month
  • You have no finished installs to photograph or ask about

FAQs About Window and Door Google Business Profile

These are the questions window and door owners ask before they hand over their profile: how it is optimized, what it costs, how verification works and how to judge a provider.

How do I optimize my Google Business Profile?

Start with the primary category, then fill every service, your hours and your service area. Add recent install photos, ask for a review after each job and reply to every review. Keep your name, address and phone number identical to your website, and check results monthly.

How do I verify my Google Business Profile?

Google asks you to prove the business is real, usually by video, phone, email or postcard, depending on what it offers for your listing. Use your exact business name and a real address or service area.

How do I get more leads from my Google Business Profile?

Reviews, photos and a complete service list drive most of it. Add a tracked phone number so you can count calls, answer during your listed hours and reply to every review. Then compare calls with booked estimates each month, not just profile views.

How do I compare Google Business Profile management providers?

Ask what is included each month, who controls the profile and how calls are tracked. Ask for a sample report that shows calls and booked estimates, not just views. Ask how suspensions are handled and whether you can leave without losing the listing.
